strategic_capability_mapping.transition: Workspace patch proposal, approval outcome, preflight snapshot, apply-plan, capability, dry-run, apply-result, and readiness-report ledger payloads move from versioned-open contracts to strict typed validation, while the unused approval-request event is explicitly payload_absent with v1 through v11 read compatibility.
strategic_capability_mapping.why_now: The remaining protocol-event-canonization blocker is full LedgerEvent payload typing. The workspace patch family is the next bounded family because it records proposal, authorization outcome, preflight, apply capability, dry-run, application result, and readiness evidence used by controlled workspace mutation replay and recovery.
strategic_capability_mapping.evidence: brownie-store validates strict WorkspacePatchProposed, WorkspacePatchApproved, WorkspacePatchRejected, WorkspacePatchPreflightSnapshotCreated, WorkspacePatchApplyPlanCreated, WorkspacePatchApplyCapabilityChecked, WorkspacePatchApplyDryRunChecked, WorkspacePatchApplyResultRecorded, and WorkspacePatchReadinessReportCreated payload fields before append/read, rejects WorkspacePatchApprovalRequested payloads as payload_absent, preserves legacy v1 through v11 payload-envelope read compatibility, and the generated semantic contract records closed status for those families.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Narrows the protocol-event-canonization release blocker with strict typed workspace patch ledger payload contracts so controlled workspace mutation replay/recovery can depend on bounded proposal and apply evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: RRP-5.16 advances protocol-event-canonization by moving workspace patch proposal, approval, rejection, preflight, apply-plan, capability, dry-run, apply-result, and readiness-report ledger event families to strict typed payload validation while preserving explicit release-blocking debt for remaining headless run/journey payload families.
answers.new_capability: New workspace patch payloads reject unknown fields, malformed field types, missing bounded proposal/preflight/apply/readiness evidence, and unbounded raw patch/file content before durable append/read; the unused WorkspacePatchApprovalRequested event is closed as payload_absent.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-5.15 made subtask orchestration and dispatch events strict typed, but workspace patch events still accepted arbitrary versioned-open payloads despite carrying replay-relevant controlled workspace mutation proposal and apply evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could still record malformed workspace patch proposal, approval, preflight, capability, dry-run, apply-result, or readiness evidence while claiming protocol-event-canonization progress.
answers.non_duplicative: This is the RRP-5.16 workspace patch event-family slice; it does not repeat RRP-5.5 inventory, RRP-5.6 known-field checks, RRP-5.7 terminal task typing, RRP-5.8 core permission typing, RRP-5.9 selected tool admission typing, RRP-5.10 MCP/tool terminal typing, RRP-5.11 Codebase Index/verification context typing, RRP-5.12 task/LLM lifecycle typing, RRP-5.13 task admission/mode-resolution typing, RRP-5.14 tool planning/intent typing, RRP-5.15 subtask orchestration/dispatch typing, RRP-7.2 durability/deadline work, or CI workflow hardening.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-5.16 adds no JSON-RPC method and only hardens durable ledger payload validation plus generated contract evidence.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The generated semantic contract and audit files are guard evidence, not a new user-facing Runtime summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Ledger appends with payloads for WorkspacePatchProposed, WorkspacePatchApproved, WorkspacePatchRejected, WorkspacePatchPreflightSnapshotCreated, WorkspacePatchApplyPlanCreated, WorkspacePatchApplyCapabilityChecked, WorkspacePatchApplyDryRunChecked, WorkspacePatchApplyResultRecorded, WorkspacePatchReadinessReportCreated now use strict schemas, reject additional fields, and validate required bounded workspace patch evidence before writing or reading; WorkspacePatchApprovalRequested rejects payloads as payload_absent until a Runtime append path exists.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless resume/replay gains stronger controlled workspace mutation evidence because workspace patch proposal, preflight, capability, dry-run, apply-result, and readiness ledgers are no longer versioned-open during new writes.
answers.milestone_progress: Narrows protocol-event-canonization from 21 to 11 release-blocking open payload families while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until remaining headless run/journey payload families, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/protocol/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not claim every LedgerEvent payload is strictly typed.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, queue, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing infrastructure, or external platform products.
Does not modify .github workflow files; runtime-release-guard-ci remains a separate blocker.
Does not reopen or alter the closed RRP-7.2 platform-deadline-durability baseline.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected docs-only closure because semantic compatibility needs generated fixtures and executable tests.
Rejected VSIX-owned schema generation because Runtime/protocol must own public wire semantics.
Rejected adding new RPCs because the closure concerns existing protocol compatibility.
technical_debt: protocol-event-canonization remains required-before-release for strict typed, payload-absent, or legacy-only schema assignments across the remaining headless continuation/run/journey LedgerEventKind payload families.
runtime-release-guard-ci remains open Runtime-owned debt until workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.
Owner license/publish/release decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue bounded strict ledger payload coverage slices until protocol-event-canonization closes, then return to runtime-release-guard-ci only when workflow-scope credentials or an owner-approved equivalent path is available.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-5.5 corrects protocol-event-canonization scope so RPC contracts and payload fingerprint split stay closed while full ledger payload typing remains required-before-release; RRP-5.6 through RRP-5.16 progressively close terminal task, permission, selected tool, MCP approval, tool terminal, Codebase Index, verification recovery context, task/LLM lifecycle, task admission/mode-resolution, tool planning/intent parsing, subtask orchestration/dispatch, and workspace patch payload families without claiming full ledger payload typing.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime blockers and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger semantics are preserved and more strictly checked.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-5.16.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-5.16.
